relevance_note: The paper reports 11 individually listed AxD probands with GFAP variants and their parents, e.g. 'The mother of proband #110 (ID#110M) revealed a mosaicism of GFAP mutation already detected in her son'.
method_note: Rows were written by a short Python script from my reading of the main text and Supplementary Table S1 (Table1.xlsx, sheet Foglio1); each transcribed cell was checked against the table. Scope: 11 probands (PROBAND ID column, bare numbers -> 'Table S1 #<n>', except proband #110, proband #147 and ID#180A, which the text labels) and their 22 tested parents (PARENTS ID column labels, e.g. '4M'; 'ID#110M' and 'ID#147F' as used in the text). Parent sex is recorded only where the text states mother/father (ID#110M, ID#147F); the M/F suffix of other parent IDs was not used to infer sex. The paper gives no clinical phenotype for any proband, so no phenotypic_features rows for probands and every checklist item is 'not reported'; parents are described as a group as 'asymptomatic', recorded only for ID#110M, who is stated individually to be asymptomatic. Zygosity 'heterozygous' and pathogenicity 'causative' for probands come from statements naming the group of 11 probands. Inheritance 'de novo' for the 10 probands other than #110 rests on parents 'without previously detected GFAP mutations' by Sanger sequencing; the authors call these 'apparently de novo', NGS results for parents other than ID#110M are not given individually (only that one parent had mosaicism), and ID#147F was not evaluable by NGS. Proband #110: mother ID#110M is a somatic (blood) mosaic for c.236G>A, inferred to be germline mosaic by the authors; recorded inheritance 'inherited maternal' and zygosity 'mosaic' for the mother. Transcript is printed as 'NM_002,055.5' (with a comma), copied verbatim. The paper says parents 'whose siblings are affected' where children are meant. Proband 4 is marked as previously published (Caroli et al., 2007). No stacked cells.
